messages.content:
A learner of Spanish is rewriting part of a post. The sentence they are working towards, for you only (never quote it or give it away): "pero no como carne). ¿Sería posible que la familia cocinara algo para mí sin carne?". Gloss each hint word in the sense it has in that sentence, not its most common sense ("alone" in "the clouds alone explain it" means "only", not "by oneself").

Their hint words, exactly 4: "posible", "carne", "preparar", "cocinar". "a / b" is a choice between two words.

For each of these hint words and no others, in this order: piece: the hint word as given. gloss: in English, what it means here and how it is used, in one or two short sentences (the kind of word, what it goes with, register if it matters; for a choice, how the two differ). example: one short, natural Spanish sentence that uses it in the same sense, about everyday life and on a topic unrelated to the post (different people, events and subject), so it shows the word without giving away the sentence they are building.
Reply with JSON only: {"notes":[{"piece":"","gloss":"","example":""}]}

result.text: {"notes":[{"piece":"posible","gloss":"Means 'possible' in the sense of whether something could happen or be done. It is used in the impersonal pattern ser posible que + subjunctive to make a polite request, roughly 'would it be possible that...'.","example":"¿Es posible llegar al estadio en metro desde aquí?"},{"piece":"carne","gloss":"Means 'meat' as a food, usually uncountable, so 'sin carne' means 'without meat' (no meat dishes). It is the general word for meat, not a specific type like pollo or pescado.","example":"La carnicería del barrio vende carne de cerdo muy barata."},{"piece":"preparar","gloss":"Not used in this sentence. It means 'to prepare or get ready' and can apply to making a dish, but here the sentence uses cocinar for cooking, so this word is not needed.","example":"Voy a preparar la mochila para el viaje de mañana."},{"piece":"cocinar","gloss":"A transitive verb meaning 'to cook' something, here in the imperfect subjunctive (cocinara) after a verb of wishing or asking, with 'para mí' showing who the food is for. It is the standard everyday verb for cooking food.","example":"Mi padre cocina arroz los domingos al mediodía."}]}
